chunks: Ibn Qulawayh from his father from Sa'd ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Is-haq ibn Ammar al-Sayrafī said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding the Fitrah? Is it permissible for me to pay it in silver at the value of these items that you mentioned?' He said, 'Yes, indeed that is more beneficial for him; he buys with it what he wishes.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitrah, the alms-tax paid at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Can Fitrah be paid in silver or money instead of specific food items?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that paying the Fitrah in silver is not only permissible but preferable, as it grants the payer the flexibility to acquire the specific food items most needed or desired. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the underlying purpose of Zakat and Fitrah—facilitating ease for the recipient—rather than rigid adherence to fixed commodities, a view supported by the concept of 'nafa'' (benefit/utility) in fiqh.
